items.title: Production RAG Chatbot (Confidential Client)
items.subtitle: Grounded FastAPI chatbot with policy routing
items.goal: Inherited a basic domain chatbot that answered loosely, missed edge cases (greetings, follow-ups, out-of-scope asks), and could not reliably capture leads. The job was to turn it into a production RAG system that stays grounded in approved knowledge, routes intents safely, validates quality before reply, and converts high-intent conversations into structured leads—without leaking proprietary product branding publicly.
items.outcome: ~45% fewer ungrounded / out-of-scope answers; ~35% higher relevance on regression scenario suites; ~30% better qualified lead completion; ~50% more failure modes caught pre-release via scenario + regression tests; ~40–50% faster iteration from requirement → hardened release using AI-assisted delivery.
items.approach: Replace “one prompt calls the model” with a modular orchestration loop owned by a FastAPI service: retrieve evidence from a vector store → classify conversational intent → generate a grounded answer (or controlled refusal/redirect) → run hard/soft validators → return typed ChatResponse with optional citations. Keep lead capture as a parallel state machine so sales collection never contaminates answer grounding. Cap session history and persist lead state per session id so multi-turn chat stays coherent and recoverable.
items.whyApproach: Domain Q&A fails when answers are ungrounded or when edge intents share the same generation path as factual replies. Explicit routing is cheaper and more testable than hoping the LLM always behaves. Pre-response validation + a soft review queue catch policy/quality slips that pure prompting misses. Separating lead extraction from RAG generation keeps prompts focused and measurable.
pipeline: Ingest & index approved knowledge into a vector store (chunking + metadata such as source family)
Retrieve top chunks with boost heuristics keyed to the user query
Route intent: greeting · follow-up rewrite · out-of-scope · curiosity redirect · grounded answer · lead flow
Generate with history context (last ~5 turns) under policy constraints
Validate hard failures vs soft review issues; log soft cases to a review queue
Format public source labels/citations for the UI; optionally append CTA when visit threshold is met
If lead threshold hits: AI field extraction → missing-field prompts → submit API when complete
components: **Orchestrator** — single chat entrypoint owning routing, history, lead branching, and response assembly
**Retriever + boost** — vector search with query-aware re-ranking heuristics
**Generator pack** — grounded answers, greeting, OOS, redirect, and follow-up query rewrite helpers
**Validators + review queue** — hard block vs soft warn with offline review logging
**Lead subsystem** — scoring, AI extraction, missing-field prompts, submit/fail statuses
**Audio/TTS path** — narration for guided visitor content pages
**React/Vite UI** — markdown answers, session cookies, safety filters, CTA surfaces
items.howBuilt: Python FastAPI routers expose typed `/chat` contracts (`ChatRequest`/`ChatResponse`). Core logic lives in an orchestrator that loads/saves lead state under a session-safe path, appends capped history, and calls retrieval → generation → validation. Source display maps internal chunks to public citation labels. Frontend is React 19 + Vite + TypeScript with markdown rendering, axios API client, and content-safety utilities. Regression/scenario test suites exercise routing and retrieval. CI runs on GitLab. TTS batch utilities generate guided-page narration assets used by the UI.
items.evals: Scenario + retrieval regression suites for routing/grounding; soft-issue review queue for production drift; typed response statuses (`lead_submitted`, quality blocks, etc.) make offline analysis and UI branching deterministic.

items.title: Generative Content RAG Backend (Confidential)
items.subtitle: FAISS-backed copy/media generation API
items.goal: Manual drafting of domain copy/creative was slow and inconsistently on-brand. Build a backend that retrieves approved knowledge before generation, enforces guidelines after generation, and returns results via async jobs so heavier media/copy work does not block clients.
items.outcome: ~60% faster content turnaround vs manual drafting; stronger policy adherence through sanitizers + guideline enforcement; reusable prompt-contract pattern (identity → input rules → taxonomy → quality → output schema) for new content types.
items.approach: Build a second RAG lane beside chat: FAISS index over curated corpora → retrieve context → assemble locked prompt templates → generate → sanitize → run guideline enforcer → persist outputs through a job queue. Keep prompt packs modular so copy vs media paths share infrastructure but not prompts.
items.whyApproach: Prompt-only generation drifts. Retrieval grounds drafts in approved material. FAISS is a strong fit for mid-size knowledge that still needs low-latency local/server search. Async jobs match CPU/GPU-heavy or multi-step creative work while letting HTTP APIs stay responsive.
pipeline: Build/rebuild FAISS index from curated knowledge sources
Accept generation request (copy and/or media) over FastAPI
Retrieve top context chunks for the brief
Fill prompt templates with identity, constraints, and schema
Generate draft → sanitize text/media descriptors
Enforce domain guideline rules; reject or rewrite on failures
Queue longer jobs; return job status + final artifacts
components: **FAISS store + index builder** — vector persistence and rebuild tooling
**Job queue / media jobs** — async execution for heavier work
items.howBuilt: Python modules for index build, FAISS store, RAG pipeline, sanitizers, guideline enforcement, storage, and media job orchestration. FastAPI routers expose copy and media APIs. Prompt text packs define ad/text and image prompts separately. Same service host as the chat backend so client products can call both lanes from one AI service footprint.
items.evals: Guideline enforcement unit checks plus manual brand review loops; job status tracking for failure visibility; sanitizers reduce unsafe/off-policy emissions before client UIs display drafts.

items.title: TwinMind
items.subtitle: Live transcription + suggestion agent
items.goal: Build a live meeting copilot: capture audio in ~30s chunks, stream transcription word-by-word to the UI, generate exactly three typed suggestion cards per segment, and support grounded chat expand/continue with independent transcript windows.
items.outcome: Working FastAPI + Next.js system with NDJSON streaming transcription, schema-locked suggestion JSON (with retry without `response_format` when providers reject JSON mode), temperature-per-task controls, and Netlify-ready frontend + separate backend hosting.
items.approach: Split client/server responsibilities hard: browser owns MediaRecorder chunking, transcript identity (`rowId` vs `chunkId`), and settings; FastAPI owns all Groq calls (Whisper + chat) so keys never live in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`. Use NDJSON streaming for transcription UX. Force suggestion outputs through schema-in-prompt + JSON mode. Keep suggestion rolling window and chat grounding window as independent minute settings.
items.whyApproach: Meetings punish latency and unstructured model output. Chunk streaming feels real-time. Strict JSON keeps the three-card UI stable. Independent context windows prevent “chat history” from polluting per-chunk suggestions (and vice versa). Server-side LLM calls are the only responsible key-handling pattern for a demo that still looks production-shaped.
pipeline: Browser records audio; every ~30s restart recorder and POST blob (skip tiny chunks under a min byte threshold)
Backend posts to Groq Whisper (`whisper-large-v3`) then streams word deltas as NDJSON
UI upserts transcript rows (stable `rowId`, monotonic `chunkId`); edits can re-trigger suggestions
POST `/api/suggestions` with chunk + optional extended transcript → exactly 3 typed cards
“Open in chat” → `/api/chat-expand`; freeform → `/api/chat-continue` with separate grounding window
Export JSON snapshot (transcript, suggestion batches, chat, settings) for review/grading
components: **Next.js dashboard** — transcript / suggestions / chat columns + Settings overrides
**Prompt contracts** — identity, input rules, taxonomy, quality rules, output JSON schema
**MarkdownLite** — lightweight chat rendering without heavy deps
items.howBuilt: Monorepo: `frontend/` (Next.js 16, React, TypeScript, Tailwind) and `backend/` (FastAPI, pydantic models, httpx). Transcription streams paced word deltas after Whisper returns. Suggestions use temperature ~0.65 and JSON mode with a compatibility retry. Chat expand/continue use lower temps (~0.5 / ~0.55). Settings persist in `localStorage`. Netlify `base=frontend`; backend deployed separately with CORS for the site origin.
items.evals: Manual latency/feel checks on streaming; JSON parse resilience via retry; UI regressions around duplicate `chunkId` rows and SSR clock mismatch handled with client-only time rendering; export artifact used for end-to-end review.

items.title: AlphaBot Trading System
items.subtitle: Backtest → walk-forward → paper/live
items.goal: Build an autonomous trading stack where research, walk-forward optimization, and live execution share one pipeline—so offline validation actually predicts production behavior—and live trading stays gated behind risk controls and an explicit cutover runbook.
items.outcome: Python 3.12 Conda environment with OHLCV parquet cache, walk-forward optimization (overfit flags when OOS Sharpe collapses vs IS), paper/live Alpaca adapters, portfolio guards, session restore, and LIVE_TRADING operational checklist.
items.approach: Architecture as a multi-agent / staged pipeline: market scan → signals → regime classification → confirmation → decision → risk/portfolio guards → broker execution → lifecycle tracking. Prefer local cached OHLCV for WFO grids (`cache_only` after prefetch) to avoid Yahoo rate limits. Run WFO on the same live pipeline code with mock sentiment during grids. Promote configs only after IS/OOS review.
items.whyApproach: Trading ML dies from train/serve skew and silent overfit. Sharing the live pipeline in backtests is the reliability answer. Walk-forward is stricter than a single split. Caching makes Windows WFO practical. Kill-switches, confirmation gates, and paper-first execution exist because finance demos that skip ops controls are not “systems engineering.”
pipeline: Prefetch OHLCV into `data/cache/ohlcv/{interval}/{SYMBOL}.parquet`
Run walk-forward grid on live pipeline (optional jobs parallelism; Windows-safe entrypoint)
Score IS vs OOS; flag OVERFITTED when Sharpe collapses >50% with positive IS
Promote strategy params into runtime settings
Orchestrator main loop: scanner cadence → signals → regime → confirmation → decisions
Portfolio allocator / rebalancer + portfolio guard risk checks
Broker adapter places/manages orders; lifecycle + decision logs persist; snapshots enable recovery
components: **Orchestrator** — startup, market calendar awareness, graceful shutdown, session restore
**Signal / decision / confirmation / regime engines** — core trade logic
**Backtest + WFO modules** — research path sharing live code
**Portfolio allocator, rebalancer, PortfolioGuard** — capital & risk layer
**Sentiment engine** — live path with mock mode for WFO
items.howBuilt: Installable Python package (`alphabot`) with `environment.yml` locked to 3.12 (Alpaca/aiohttp/PyYAML build constraints on Windows). YAML settings + `.env` secrets. pytest for WFO/live pipeline tests. Structured logging and decision stores for auditability. Documented live cutover (`CONFIRM_LIVE`, kill-switch drills, risk ramp).
items.evals: WFO JSON/Heatmap reports; overfit flag heuristic; pytest coverage on walk-forward live pipeline; paper trading before live keys; preflight validates Alpaca keys only when live mode is on.

items.title: Personal Chatbot-RAG
items.subtitle: Offline FAISS index + HF query embeds + Groq — powers the live portfolio chat
items.goal: Build a personal knowledge chatbot with real semantic retrieval that still deploys on free-tier hosts—without shipping PyTorch/sentence-transformers wheels that blow disk limits—and wire it into this portfolio so visitors can ask about skills, projects, and experience.
items.outcome: Slim Dockerized Flask RAG on Render: curated knowledge.json → offline HF embeddings → committed FAISS index; runtime HF query embeds + top-k retrieval + Groq (openai/gpt-oss-20b) grounded answers. Live Next.js Chatbot.jsx posts to /receive on the same service.
items.approach: Split build vs serve hard. Offline: structure-aware chunking of knowledge.json, embed with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via HF Inference API, write FAISS + chunks into the repo. Online: embed the user question the same way, FAISS similarity search, inject only retrieved chunks into a Groq prompt (openai/gpt-oss-20b). Keep Render deps to Flask, faiss-cpu, httpx, and Groq—no local embedding model. Portfolio UI owns the chat surface; Render owns retrieval + generation.
items.whyApproach: Free-tier disk killed local sentence-transformers/PyTorch installs. Prompt-stuffing the whole KB worked as a stopgap but is not RAG. Offline index + remote query embeds keep true retrieval and a portable Docker image that fits Render while staying grounded on curated profile facts.
pipeline: Curate data/knowledge.json (skills, experience, projects; exclude confidential client internals)
Chunk with structure-aware builders + projects/experience index chunks for listing queries
Offline embed via HF Inference API (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and save FAISS under data/faiss_index/
At runtime: embed question via HF → FAISS top-k → build grounded prompt → Groq generate
Serve Flask /receive + /health inside Docker; Next.js portfolio Chatbot.jsx posts to the Render URL
components: **Knowledge pack** — curated knowledge.json as source of truth
**HF embed client** — httpx calls to Inference API (build + query)
**FaissRetriever** — L2-normalized similarity search over committed vectors
**Next.js chatbot client** — embedded portfolio UX calling Render
**Dockerfile** — slim Python image with faiss-cpu (no PyTorch)
items.howBuilt: Python package under rag/ (chunking, embeddings, retriever) plus Flask app.py. Index is rebuilt locally after knowledge edits and committed so production never downloads embedding weights. Env: GROQ_API_KEY, HF_API_TOKEN, optional GROQ_MODEL / RAG_TOP_K. Deployed on Render (chatbot-rag-mun6); portfolio Chatbot.jsx calls /receive. JD matcher on the site reuses the same skill/project taxonomy for recruiter workflows.
items.evals: Manual Q&A against known profile facts (list-all-projects, specific project deep-dives); retrieval checks that projects-index ranks first on aggregate queries; /health smoke for FAISS load; container rebuild to keep the slim dependency set under free-tier disk; live chat smoke from the portfolio UI.

items.title: E-commerce RAG Agent
items.subtitle: Clean → embed → Redis semantic search
items.goal: Enable semantic product Q&A over noisy Amazon electronics FAQ/text by cleaning aggressively first, then retrieving with normalized MiniLM embeddings stored in Redis.
items.outcome: Batch ingestion with HTML/URL/email scrubbing, unicode normalization, dedupe, batch-32 embeddings (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), Redis JSON docs with vectors, and FastAPI API scaffold for phase-2 retrieval.
items.approach: Make retrieval a data-quality problem first. Clean every text field (HTML tags, entities, URLs, emails, special chars, unicode), drop empties/dupes, concatenate fields per row, embed with normalized MiniLM vectors, and store in Redis under prefixed keys for cosine similarity search.
items.whyApproach: Retail text is hostile to embeddings when HTML/noise remains. MiniLM (384-d, ~80MB) is the right speed/quality tradeoff for FAQ search. Redis is an easy online store for demos without standing up a full vector DB cluster.
pipeline: Read CSV with multi-encoding fallback (utf-8 → latin-1 → …)
Remove empty rows + duplicates
clean_text on every string field
Batch encode texts (size 32) with normalize_embeddings=True
Write `{id, embedding, ...fields}` JSON docs to Redis
Expose FastAPI retrieval/generation in phase 2
components: **SentenceTransformer MiniLM** — HF auth via env token
**FastAPI scaffold** — API surface for retrieval phase
items.howBuilt: Python ingestion script with explicit cleaning helpers, Redis client load path, `.env` for HF/Redis/CSV config, docker-compose for Redis, and requirements locking torch/sentence-transformers/onnx runtime style deps for local runs.
items.evals: Count deltas logged at each cleaning stage; Redis ping + batch load progress; manual semantic spot checks on product questions after ingestion.

items.title: AutoDoc-AI

pipeline: Upload PDF in Streamlit (document summarization mode)
Extract text with pdfplumber; detect financial vs general doc type
Chunk long documents for model context limits
Run Hugging Face prompt chain for exec summary, findings, highlights, analysis, recommendations
Render LaTeX template → optional PDF compile (Tectonic/TeX)

items.howBuilt: Python pipeline with pdfplumber extraction, HF API prompt chain, Streamlit UI for upload/run, and LaTeX templates compiled to PDF when a TeX engine is available.

items.title: DocReporter
items.subtitle: Layout-aware document reporting pipeline
items.goal: Parse complex 200+ page PDFs with layout awareness and produce concise structured reports with visuals—without forcing everything through a single brittle script.

items.whyApproach: Heavy document pipelines stall as monoliths. Layout-aware parsing beats plain text extraction for charts/tables; workflow orchestration is the reliability layer for multi-stage jobs.
pipeline: Ingest long PDFs into the document store
Airflow DAG triggers parse/layout extraction jobs
Process/enrich extracted structure
Report service renders concise structured summary + charts
Store/export artifacts for reviewers
items.howBuilt: Docker Compose multi-app setup (`analyst_app`, `process_app`, `report_app`), Airflow DAGs under `dags/`, document stores, and report services that emit human-readable summaries with charts.
items.evals: Pipeline run success via Airflow task states; qualitative review that charts/tables survive better than plain-text baselines.

items.title: MarketCanvas-Env (RL + MCP)
items.subtitle: Semantic canvas env for banner layout agents
items.goal: Build a deterministic Mini-Canva style environment where RL policies and LLM/MCP agents learn marketing-banner layout under explicit prompt constraints (headline, CTA, contrast), with bounded rewards that resist trivial hacking.
items.outcome: Gym-style env with semantic JSON observations, high-level actions, dense/terminal reward modes, WCAG contrast term (>=4.5), anti-duplication penalties, MCP tool interface, and a writeup covering PPO scaling to ~10k VLM rollouts.
items.approach: Prefer semantic actions (add/move/recolor) and JSON state (bbox, colors, overlaps, centering flags) over pixel mouse control early. Shape reward as weighted constraints (0.40) + aesthetics (0.25) + accessibility (0.25) + anti-hacking (0.10). Expose MCP for interactive agents while keeping direct Gym stepping for training throughput.
items.whyApproach: Early RL learns faster with smaller action spaces and interpretable state. Keyword gaming still exists, but duplication penalties block the cheapest exploits. Dual MCP/Gym interfaces separate demo interoperability from actor-learner training paths.
pipeline: Reset env with prompt constraints (required headline/CTA/color rules)
Agent selects semantic actions: add_element / move / change_color
Env updates JSON state (geometry, overlaps, centering, content)
Compute dense or terminal reward with WCAG + anti-duplication terms
Optional RGB render for VLM observations; MCP for tool-based interaction
items.howBuilt: Python packages for observation/action/reward/canvas env, optional PIL RGB renderer for multimodal experiments, MCP tool responses for agent tooling, and a detailed writeup on vectorizing envs / observation tiering for large parallel VLM rollouts.
items.evals: Reward bounded in [-1, 1]; known loopholes documented (keyword gaming, alignment inflation); anti-dupe tanh saturation tested conceptually against identical CTA spam.

Vectorize + reduce with PCA
Cluster (K-Means) and extract pink-slime vs legitimate signatures
Report cluster diagnostics for downstream classifiers

items.evals: Observed ~3× sentiment exaggeration patterns in pink slime vs legitimate journalism; cluster interpretability reviewed qualitatively across topic categories.
